simple.meaning: נוּם (nûwm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to slumber (from drowsiness).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Psalms, Isaiah, Nahum, beginning at Psalms 76:6. Its contexts include kingship, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נוּם (H5123).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נוּם (nûwm) / H5123 is traced through Psalms 76:6, Psalms 121:3, Psalms 121:4, Isaiah 5:27 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: At your rebuke, God of Jacob,

timeline.evidenceText: At your rebuke, God of Jacob,
He will not allow your foot to be moved.
No one shall be weary nor stumble among them;
Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
